title: Trust, provenance, and benchmark-integrity hardening — August 2026 competitive research findings
description:
Distinct from EPIC-6 (root-caused this SDK's own with-SDK vs. flat-context retrieval-quality gap, Done) and EPIC-7 (Mem0/Microsoft Agent Framework/Oracle pipeline-mechanics research, Done) — this epic is grounded in the 2026-08-03 refresh of ai-agent-platform-competitive-analysis.md (see its 'August 2026 update note' at the top and the new arXiv entries added to the Research Papers section), which surfaced findings the prior two research passes couldn't have: a new memory-poisoning attack targeting an agent's *stored reasoning traces* rather than stored facts (Karamchandani et al., 'Your Agent's Memories Are Not Its Own' / FARMA-SENTINEL, arXiv 2607.05029, July 6 2026), reaching 100% attack success against pre-existing defenses on the systems it tested; a new sycophancy-in-memory benchmark distinct from recall-accuracy benchmarks like LongMemEval/LOCOMO (MemSyco-Bench, arXiv 2607.01071, July 2026); two reproducibility rebuttals of vendor-reported memory-system benchmark gains — one direct ('Reproducing LightMem: Naive RAG Is Just as Good for Memory Management', arXiv 2607.29104, July 31 2026, showing embedding/retriever choice alone swings accuracy 58.1%→75.5% and that naive RAG matches LightMem's constructed memories at equal retrieval depth) and one earlier but newly incorporated into the doc (the MemPalace audit, arXiv 2604.21284, finding a headline 96.6% Recall@5 was mostly attributable to the default embedding model, not the claimed architecture); and Mem0's July 10 2026 'token-efficient memory algorithm' blog post reporting LongMemEval 94.4 / LOCOMO 92.5 at ~7K tokens/query via single-pass extraction — a concrete external efficiency figure this SDK has never measured itself against.

Confirmed via direct code review before scoping: this SDK has no first-class provenance/trust field on any memory record today (grepping models.py finds 'source' used exactly once, as a free-form example key inside a metadata dict on a docstring — not a governed field), and its three existing pluggable write-time hooks (Consolidator, Reconciler, IngestResolver — types.py) cover derivation, SemanticFact contradiction/supersession, and ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP classification respectively, but none of them run an integrity/anomaly check on write *content*, and none apply specifically to ProceduralMemory — this SDK's closest existing analogue to the 'stored reasoning trace' the FARMA/SENTINEL paper attacks (models.py's own docstring: 'The agent recalls these before executing a task class to apply previously learned strategies'). TRU-1/TRU-2 close that gap the same opt-in, developer-controlled way every prior epic has (Step 0 philosophy: Db2-only, zero mandatory new infrastructure, no hook fires unless the developer wires it in). TRU-3/TRU-4/TRU-5 extend PH-6's benchmarking harness (EPIC-5, scripts/run_benchmarks.py) and BENCHMARKS.md with the three concrete, actionable pieces of the August research: a sycophancy/contradiction-tracking evaluation category, a reproducibility self-check applying the exact LightMem/MemPalace critique to this SDK's own Run B 'SDK beats flat-context' claim, and a first real run of the already-built-but-never-executed Suite 2 latency/cost harness (BENCHMARKS.md's own 'Not yet run' note under Suite 2/Suite 3) so a token-efficiency figure exists to compare against Mem0's new number.

Every finding cited above is quoted or paraphrased directly from the '[Update, Aug 2026]' annotations added to ai-agent-platform-competitive-analysis.md on 2026-08-03 — see that file for full source URLs and the caveats it already flags (the new arXiv IDs use the 2607.xxxxx July-2026 numbering convention and were not independently cross-checked against a second source; treat as needing re-verification before external-facing use, same as that document's own stated policy). See the dated 2026-08-04 DECISIONS.md entry for the complete rationale, including what was deliberately left out of scope: no attempt to port MemMachine's Neo4j-specific ground-truth-preservation mechanism, and no filesystem-based-memory architecture change per the 'Filesystem-Based Memory for LLM Agents' paper (arXiv 2607.26637) — both are structurally foreign to this SDK's Db2-relational design, not a gap in it. Also out of scope: chasing any of the unverified vendor-blog LongMemEval leaderboard claims (Mastra 94.87%, OMEGA 95.4%, 'agentmemory V4' 96.2%) cited in the doc — none are peer-reviewed and the doc itself says to treat them as marketing pending independent verification.

TRU-1 and TRU-2 are sequential (TRU-2 needs the provenance field TRU-1 adds). TRU-3, TRU-4, and TRU-5 are independent of TRU-1/TRU-2 and of each other — safe to run as parallel subagents alongside the TRU-1→TRU-2 chain.
